findings.evidence:
console.debug(`webhook ${event.id} dropped after ${MAX_ATTEMPTS} attempts`);
return false;
findings.recommendation: When a merchant's endpoint is down or answers 5xx for all five attempts, the event is dropped and the only trace is a `console.debug` prose line, which production log levels typically discard and which the log platform cannot query; the listener also ignores the `false` returned by `deliver`, so the merchant silently never learns the payment settled and no operator is alerted. A non-ok response (`response.ok` false) is not logged at all, so its status code is lost. Use the project's structured `logger` from `src/logger.ts`: `logger.warn` per failed attempt with fields `eventId`, `attempt`, `status` (or `error: String(error)`), and `logger.error` when the event is dropped, with `eventId`, `paymentId` and `attempts`. Log the merchant host rather than the full URL, in case it carries a token.
findings.title: A dropped webhook is logged only at debug level, in free text

findings.recommendation: The loop starts the next attempt as soon as the previous one fails: when a merchant's server is overloaded or restarting and answers 503, the five POSTs hit it back to back within milliseconds, add load at the worst moment, and all fail inside the same outage window, so the event is dropped even though a retry a few seconds later would have succeeded. Space the attempts with exponential backoff and jitter (for example 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, 8 s), and retry only on network errors, 429 and 5xx, not on other 4xx. Because `publish` in `src/events.ts` awaits each listener in turn, sleeping inside this loop would hold the payment service's `publish` call; run the retries off that path (a queue or a scheduled retry) rather than awaiting them in the listener.
findings.title: Failed deliveries are retried immediately, with no backoff
